before: record Result(string Name, int Score) declares a record class with those named properties. It supplies value-based equality: these simple records compare their property values, not just object identity.

A with expression creates a copy with selected properties changed. It does not change the original record. Positional record-class properties are normally init-only: set at initialization rather than freely assigned afterward.
A record class is still a reference type. with performs a shallow copy: a referenced mutable collection inside a record could remain shared. This example contains only a string and an integer.
Expected behavior from this example: 3 then 5 then True. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer task: Create another Result with different Name but the same Score and compare it with first. Use a .NET 10 console project with C# 14; reading completion does not verify this local work.
after: A record is a type suited to grouped data. This record class has Name and Score properties. Its short declaration creates properties that are normally set when a record is made.
with creates a copy with selected properties changed. It does not replace those properties on the original record.
These records compare their property values. Two separate Result objects with the same name and score compare equal.
The program prints 3, then 5, then True. The original score stays 3, the copy has 5, and the final record matches the original data.

A record class is still a reference type. with makes a shallow copy: it copies each stored value without also copying every object reached through it. A mutable list inside a record could therefore remain shared.
